judged_text: The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT on the token-refresh request path has no timeout, no response.ok/status check, and no payload-size bound. If the sync endpoint hangs, every booking involving a shared credential stalls indefinitely (all callers await this promise with no AbortController); if it returns a non-JSON error page, downstream parsers throw an unrelated 500, masking the real failure.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` it does `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams(...) })` and immediately returns the `response` without any timeout/AbortController, without checking `response.ok`/status, and without guarding/parsing the body. Callers then treat the returned value as if it were a normal token-refresh response (e.g., `Office365CalendarService` passes it to `handleErrorsJson(response)` which will attempt to parse JSON; `GoogleCalendarService` expects `res?.data`). A hanging sync endpoint will stall awaiting callers indefinitely, and non-JSON error bodies will surface as generic parsing/500 errors, masking the real upstream failure.
